title: Dealing with the monster that carries a bomb
target: How to read the monster that attacks with a bomb in R.E.P.O.: the effects and voice lines are separate, the fuse tells, ignites and loops on a curve, and being stunned or attacking are split into their own sounds.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Sound you can hear over the level
A route out of the room

steps.do: Listen for the fuse rather than watching the bomb, because the tell, the ignition and the burning loop each have their own sound.
steps.because: the fuse has a tell, an ignite and a loop of its own (soundFuseTell, soundFuseIgnite, soundFuseLoop)

steps.do: Give the loop a curve rather than a steady volume, because the burning sound is played on one.
steps.because: the fuse loop is played on a curve of its own (soundFuseLoopCurve)

steps.do: Treat the explosion tell as the last warning you get.
steps.because: there is a separate sound for the tell before the explosion (soundExplosionTell)

steps.do: Know that the monster speaks and thumps separately, because deaths, jumps and landings each have an effect and a voice line.
steps.because: deaths, jumps and landings each have an effect sound and a voice line (soundDeathSFX, soundDeathVO, soundJumpSFX, soundJumpVO, soundLandSFX, soundLandVO)

steps.do: Read its approach from the short and long move sounds and the footstep.
steps.because: it has a short move, a long move and a footstep sound (soundMoveShort, soundMoveLong, soundFootstep)

steps.do: Judge a hit by its weight, because light, medium and heavy impacts sound different.
steps.because: impacts are split into light, medium and heavy (soundImpactLight, soundImpactMedium, soundImpactHeavy)

steps.do: Know that an attack is announced by a breaker rather than by the voice alone.
steps.because: attacks run through their own breaker (soundAttackBreaker)

steps.do: Expect the idle noise to be broken up as well.
steps.because: the idle noise has a breaker of its own (soundIdleBreaker)

steps.do: Treat a stun as three sounds, because being stunned has an introduction, a loop and an outro.
steps.because: being stunned has an intro, a loop and an outro (soundStunIntro, soundStunLoop, soundStunOutro)

steps.do: Do not trust your own ears for volume, because the monster's output can be scaled as a whole.
steps.because: the monster carries a volume multiplier for its sounds (enemy, controller, volumeMultiplier)

commonMistakes: Watching the bomb and missing the fuse tell.
Hearing the fuse and assuming it is already lit, when ignition is a separate sound.
Treating a jump or a landing as one noise instead of an effect plus a voice.
Relaxing during a stun because only the start was noticed.
Ignoring the idle breaker and reading a pause as the monster leaving.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
